speechtext: Mr. Speaker, the Hon. Member for Burin-St. George's (Mr. Simmons) said that he puts his money where his mouth is. I want to know how much money he has.

subsubtopic: ALLOTTED DAY, S.O. 62-NON-CONFIDENCE MOTION-YOUTH EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I am delighted to answer that question. I want to draw attention to the concluding remarks I made which are now reinforced by the question and the questioner. While we believe that serious things need to be done on a continuing basis to provide more jobs for youth, the Hon. Member's approach to the problem is to prove that if he is not witty, he is at least half-witty.

subsubtopic: ALLOTTED DAY, S.O. 62-NON-CONFIDENCE MOTION-YOUTH EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, in the first part of the Hon. Member's speech he referred to what the benefit of an agreement on the offshore of Newfoundland would be to the employment picture in Newfoundland. Can the Hon. Member explain to this House why the Government of Newfoundland was unwilling to accept the revenue sharing offer made to the Government of Newfoundland by the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources (Mr. Chretien) in the same terms which the Government of Nova Scotia was quite ready and willing to accept? Could he tell us what benefit that would have in terms of jobs to Newfoundland?

subsubtopic: ALLOTTED DAY, S.O. 62-NON-CONFIDENCE MOTION-YOUTH EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES
speechtext:
I thank my friend from Miramichi for his question. He is right, of course. There was an offer made by the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources (Mr. Chretien). He calls to mind the distinction I made in my speech between the Government of Newfoundland as a whole and the Leader of that Government, Mr. Peckford. It is well known because it was documented on the national news that day.
The Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources and Mr. Marshall went before national television cameras to say they
Supply
were pleased with the outcome of the meeting, that they essentially had an agreement and that they just wanted to take it back to their respective governments. Within a few hours the Premier of Newfoundland was on the radio basically saying, "Not so fast, we don't have an agreement yet". He was scared to death that they might have an agreement. They almost had it, to the credit of Mr. Marshall and the Minister of Energy. They were so near that they went public with their accord; they announced it on national television.
I just want to correct my good friend, the Hon. Member for Northumberland-Miramichi (Mr. Dionne), in one respect. He said that it was a deal somewhat like the one offered to Nova Scotia. He is wrong, only in the sense that it was a deal considerably better than the one offered to Nova Scotia. I mean no offence to Nova Scotians, but we in Newfoundland have learned that if we bargain long and hard enough we will get an even better deal than the other fellows, and that is the deal which the Minister of Energy offered Mr. Marshall.

subsubtopic: ALLOTTED DAY, S.O. 62-NON-CONFIDENCE MOTION-YOUTH EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, in his opening comments the Hon. Member perceived what was happening when I asked questions of the Hon. Member who spoke prior to him. When the Progressive Conservative Party was in office, it stated as its policy that there would be no direct job-creation programs from the federal Government, that that was the business of private enterprise, and that it would try to help out private enterprise.
I believe the Government of Canada should not only maintain but increase the amount of money going into the Summer Student Employment Program. In doing away with all direct job-creation programs, the Conservatives would see that program go down the drain. There would be no student jobs under it if they were in office again.
Would the Hon. Member explain to the House briefly the importance of that program which the Conservatives do not like and would not have in existence if they were in power? Would he explain to the House the types of accomplishments and the types of people who would work under that program? Could he indicate to the House whether or not they would have summer jobs if this federal Government program did not exist?

subsubtopic: ALLOTTED DAY, S.O. 62-NON-CONFIDENCE MOTION-YOUTH EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the Hon. Member for Gander-Twillingate focused very well on yet another reason; whatever our loyalty to this Party of which we are a part, we have a greater loyalty to the youth of Canada. We have to get out there and do our utmost to ensure that the crowd which would rob them of the few available jobs never get into office. He says it so well that he fires me up even more to get out there and ensure that the people of Canada understand what is a pig in a poke when they are asked to vote Tory.
Concerning his question about the Summer Canada Program, I cannot think of any better job-creation program in existence. When I travel through my riding, I see them helping the aged. I see them repairing roads in small communities which have no vehicular traffic. I see them out with shovels and wheelbarrows. I see them improving slipways and

wharves. I see them doing things which add to the improvement of communities. I see them learning good job skills. I see them earning money so that they can attend university, return to high school or participate in funding the family budget, as meagre as it may be in some of those communities. I believe in that particular program. I shudder when I think of a day that it might be wiped out because of the rhetoric of some people about private enterprise who have no feeling in their guts about the youth of their country who desperately need that money and more of it.
